Scope: `custody_elective_allocation`.

# Two-series elective exchange contract

All cash figures are integer USD cents. The client owns one pool of old shares. A unit tendered to either series is locked against that offer and unavailable for an old-share delivery or the other offer until its actual allotment. Each offer accepts one irrevocable positive tender by minute zero, in its recorded tender_increment and up to its own maximum_tender_units. The combined tender must fit the actually available old shares and wallet. An offer may be left unelected, producing zero allotment. Each tender immediately transfers units times subscription_price_minor out of available cash into that series' subscription escrow. This is maximum subscription funding, not a charge or the final number of new shares. It cannot be borrowed, withdrawn or reused before that series' allotment.

The series have independent published possible_acceptance_bp values. Their actual values are not available until their separate allotment events. At allotment, accepted old shares equal floor(tendered_units times actual_acceptance_bp divided by 10,000). Exactly that many old shares are surrendered and the same number of that series' new shares are delivered. The issuer consumes accepted_units times subscription_price_minor from escrow. Unaccepted old shares and unused escrow are returned at that event. Acceptance cannot be rejected afterward. Old shares returned by the later event were unavailable for earlier delivery. Neither a query nor request preparation accelerates allotment.

The existing sale requires actual old-share delivery and its independent invoice payment by the recorded deadline. Delivery irreversibly consumes available old shares. The bank permits an authorized partial or excess delivery or invoice payment; meeting the customer's contract depends on the final exact quantities and actual times. The invoice is payable only from free wallet cash.

Series A and B have distinct new shares and customer acquisition deadlines. New A shares cannot satisfy the B target, or vice versa. The customer may need a secondary purchase after a short allotment or a sale after an excess allotment. Market routes specify class, opening and closing minute, minimum and maximum quantity, quantity increment, and separate buy and sell prices. BLOCK requires a multiple of eight shares and has a lower purchase price. ODD accepts one to seven shares after opening. Every execution must independently fit one route's lot terms; several genuine executions are allowed. A purchase debits its price times quantity and credits new shares. A sale credits its sell price times quantity and consumes already available new shares; short sales are unavailable. Spread costs cannot be recovered. Settlement is immediate. The A allotment also issues one bonus right for every complete source_divisor accepted A shares. Market purchases do not create these rights. Each right can be redeemed for its recorded cash redemption amount, or exercised for its recorded number of B shares against the subscription cash price. Exercise is available only under a joint application with an actual B tender submitted by the original offer deadline; otherwise cash redemption remains available. This eligibility survives the B allotment. The rights are genuine consumable subscription entitlements: each exercised or redeemed right is deducted from remaining_units, and all rights must be settled by their deadline. Their optional early redemption is irreversible. Rights exercise can produce more B shares than the customer ultimately wants, and ordinary market sales of that excess remain permitted. These rights are independent of the later B allotment and do not reduce that allotment. The transfer-agent invoice is a separate cash obligation with its own due minute. There are no other market routes, lending facilities, offer cancellation services or outside funds. Acquisition deadlines are inclusive, and a later trade cannot repair an earlier missed target. Final available cash excludes all still-held escrow.

Unlock propose_custody_election. Every instruction contains case_id, action and data. elect data is {record_id: offer ID, units: positive integer}; deliver_old data is {units: positive integer}; pay_invoice data is {amount_minor: positive integer}; market_trade data is {record_id: market route ID, side: BUY or SELL, units: positive integer}. redeem_rights and exercise_rights data is {units: positive integer rights}; pay_registrar_fee data is {amount_minor: positive integer}. Proposals do not reserve shares or cash. The owner approves each exact request before execute_request. Assess execution against current records, including previous actual tenders and allotments.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_custody_election`

Prepare an elective exchange tender, old-share delivery, invoice payment, bonus-right redemption or subscription, or a class-specific block or odd-lot market trade.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
